source_text: Regarding the mission and the dilemma between most of the elaborator and a small generic core, we have been trying to compile a blank file, and if that requires most of the elaborator that is the fault of Lean's design not our port.

fragments.text: Regarding the mission and the dilemma between most of the elaborator and a small generic core, we have been trying to compile a blank file, and if that requires most of the elaborator that is the fault of Lean's design not our port.

reply_text:
㊥ (the blank file and the elaborator) I agree with most of that. The size of the subset is set by how Lean's own source is written, not by anything the port got wrong, and my earlier wording should not be read as faulting the port. There is one distinction I would keep, about where the need for an elaborator comes from.

㊟ (what a blank file needs versus what the port needs) Native Lean processing a blank file hardly uses the term elaborator: it parses the header and sets up an empty environment. The elaborator comes in because the port obtains that parser and environment code by compiling its Lean source. That source is written in full Lean, with type classes, monads, notation and default instances, so compiling it means elaborating it. I take your point that this is Lean's doing: the parser is not written in a small subset.

㊬ (how Lean itself handles this) Lean has the same dependency and does not solve it by elaborating from source. Your `lean4` checkout has `stage0/stdlib/Lean/Parser/*.c` and `stage0/stdlib/Lean/Elab/*.c`: the parser and elaborator shipped as already-elaborated, generated C. This is the C that the mission's 2026-08-24 rule names as the behavioural authority.

㊟ (what follows for the plan) Whoever's fault it is, the estimate is the same: the 110 rows will need whichever elaborator steps their source uses, and so far those are being found one failed probe at a time. Under your "same technology" condition, I would put the effort into finding them sooner. That is what S3 and S4 in claude-4's list are for.

㊭ (measure the subset instead of discovering it) The set of elaborator steps the 110 rows need is finite, and native Lean can report it in advance. Elaborating just those declarations with elaborator tracing on would list which steps run (default instances, coercions, postponement, and so on) and for which rows. That gives a checklist to compare against what the port has, and a number in place of my "most of the elaborator". Your `lean-dyncov` repository does the same kind of measurement for the compiler passes, so the method is already in the house; I have not checked how much of it carries over to elaborator traces.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I pass that measurement idea to claude-4 as a discovery packet proposal, alongside S4?
